idiom_name: Codable conformance with CodingKeys and JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder
implementation_notes: Codable is a typealias for the two-direction pair - Encodable.encode(to:) and Decodable.init(from:) - so conformance (usually synthesized) makes a type convertible to and from an external representation, while JSONEncoder/JSONDecoder or PropertyListEncoder supply the format side and never see the type's internals. CodingKeys and the encoders' strategy options pin the wire contract; custom init(from:)/encode(to:) replace the classic converter class when the derived shape is wrong, and a separate DTO is the better answer when one type needs two wire shapes.
pitfalls: Encoder and decoder strategies must match: a decoder left at .deferredToDate fails on dates the encoder wrote as ISO-8601.
Adding a stored property breaks decoding of existing payloads unless it is optional or read with decodeIfPresent.
keyDecodingStrategy (for example .convertFromSnakeCase) applies recursively and interacts with hand-written CodingKeys, silently changing the contract.
Synthesized conformance ignores computed properties and property wrappers without explicit support, so what is encoded is not always what the type exposes.

variants.name: RawRepresentable (rawValue + init?(rawValue:))
variants.implementation_notes: For a single-value representation the standard library supplies the pair directly: rawValue gives value to representation and init?(rawValue:) gives representation to value, synthesized for enums with a raw type and implementable by any struct or class. It is the right shape for identifiers, codes and unit-bearing scalars whose external form is one primitive; it carries no structure, no versioning and a nil rather than an error, so structured or versioned payloads belong to Codable or a DTO.
pitfalls: init?(rawValue:) is failable by contract and callers must handle nil; a non-failable initializer hides invalid external input.
A type that validates in init?(rawValue:) must enforce the same rule in every other initializer, or instances exist that cannot be represented.
Conforming a class with a mutable rawValue to RawRepresentable breaks value semantics (equality, hashing, use as a dictionary key).
